paper_ref: CAPRISE paper Fig. 5 / PAPER_ANALYSIS.md Section 9.5 (ambiguities A12, A13, A19)

definition.ASR@t: |top_t(ciphertext distances) & top_t(plaintext distances)| / t, averaged over queries; lower = more privacy
definition.kendall: Kendall tau between the full plaintext and ciphertext distance vectors (m-1 entries; lower = less leakage)
definition.spearman: Spearman rho between the same two vectors (lower = less leakage)
definition.dist_err: mean |d_cipher/s - d_plain| over all pairs; lower bound on absolute-distance leakage (scale removed)
definition.attack_query: one stored ciphertext e'_j from the encrypted database (server-visible), NOT an EncQ ciphertext

setup.note: d=768 real = gtr-t5-base MS MARCO passage embeddings (L2 normalised); d=1536/3072 synthetic = L2-normalised i.i.d. Gaussian (GTR emits only 768 dims, A13); a synthetic d=768 control makes the dimension trend distribution-consistent.

selfcheck.description: E' = s*E (no noise): ciphertext ranking must equal plaintext ranking

corpus_composition.note: row order = [qrels-relevant passages sorted by pid] + [BM25 hard negatives sorted by pid] + [random filler sorted by pid]; any corpus prefix of length >= qrels_relevant+bm25_hard_neg contains all relevant passages. Passages.jsonl carries a per-row 'source' field and data/corpus_sources.npy matches it.

findings.interpretation: ASR@10 is essentially invariant to m on real GTR in [2000, 50000] (ADCPE 0.956-0.964, CAPRISE 0.935-0.947) although the mean plaintext NN distance falls from 0.80 to 0.65; database density therefore does not explain the residual gap between our real-GTR ASR and the paper's digitised 87.5% / 83.1% at d=768.  Our controlled synthetic d=768 point (88.2 / 83.2) matches the paper's 768 bar almost exactly, so the difference is a real-vs-synthetic embedding geometry effect, not a database-size effect.  The paper does not state m for Fig. 5, so its absolute ASR level is not identifiable (A12/A13).
unnormalised vectors make the fixed noise radius negligible at large d (ASR->1); this cannot reproduce the paper's low ASR at small dimensions, so A4 is not the explanation of the paper's trend.
